From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: ops@veridianhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime feed: client-visible silence on 11/12 — urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Ingress proxies in us-west-2 show bursty egress queues between 07:50–08:05; packets delayed 150–800ms before forwarding.
- Kernel tcp_write_wakeups spike on two proxy hosts (proxy-023, proxy-027) after a rolling kernel hotspot patch earlier this week.
- Our streaming chunker process shows GC pauses correlated with those timestamps on one shard.

Immediate mitigation proposed:
1) Flip affected customer routing to the dedicated serving pool (grace can do) — avoids the shared proxy path causing coalescing delays.
2) Temporarily increase proxy egress worker threads on proxy-023/027 and disable aggressive coalescing (config flag chunk_coalesce_ms -> 0).
3) If that does not stabilize within 30m, failover Veridian to the non-streaming (polling) endpoint as emergency fallback.

I'll open SERV-4821 and attach the initial logs. Pushing a small RB to proxy hosts now.

-Markus
SRE Lead
[Attachment: veridian_network_logs.tar.gz (log archive)]

Team —

Short exec note to prep for potential board mention and customer C-suite outreach. Please review and flag changes.
Summary:
- Impact: Veridian (tier-1 customer) experienced streaming chunk silence between 07:55–08:30 PST causing degraded experiences for ~8% of calls; similar pattern observed in 2 other customers (internal sampling).
- Root cause (preliminary): proxy egress queuing combined with chunk coalescing and GC pause on a shard after this week's kernel patch. SERV-4821 opened.
- Mitigation taken: routed Veridian to veridian-dedicated-usw, disabled tenant coalescing, increased proxy worker threads; observed latency back to baseline for Veridian after cutover.
- Risk: if not fully mitigated, potential SLA breach exposure and churn risk for affected customers. Recommend preparing a one-time credit up to 5% of monthly invoice for Veridian and a short formal RCA within 72h.

Requested decisions:
1) Approve temporary customer credit up to 5% (yes/no).
2) Approve a coordinated external communication (Ben to draft).
3) Board mention approval if credit/contract impact exceeds $75k.

Attachments: slo export attached and incident timeline. Links: SERV-4821, drive folder with logs.

-David
Director, Customer Reliability
